title: Accessible and presentable infinity categories
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all quasicategories below fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use simplicial sets and nondegenerate simplices from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and spaces, quasicategories, equivalences, mapping spaces, coherent diagrams, cocones and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a simplicial set is $\kappa$-small if its set of nondegenerate simplices has cardinality less than $\kappa$. A quasicategory $I$ is $\kappa$-filtered if every coherent diagram $K\to I$ for a $\kappa$-small simplicial set $K$ admits a cocone; $K=\varnothing$ is included. A quasicategory $\mathcal C$ is locally small if each mapping space is equivalent to a small space. It admits small $\kappa$-filtered colimits if all diagrams indexed by small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategories have colimits.

When these colimits exist, an object $c\in\mathcal C$ is $\kappa$-compact if the functor $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,-)$ to spaces preserves them: for every such diagram $F:I\to\mathcal C$, the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,F(i))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,\operatorname{colim}_I F)$ is an equivalence of spaces. The category $\mathcal C$ is $\kappa$-accessible if it is locally small, admits small $\kappa$-filtered colimits and has an essentially small full subcategory of $\kappa$-compact objects such that every object of $\mathcal C$ is a colimit of a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram taking values in that subcategory. Essentially small means equivalent to a small quasicategory. Accessible means $\kappa$-accessible for some infinite regular $\kappa\in\mathcal U$. Presentable means accessible and admitting colimits of all diagrams indexed by small simplicial sets. A coherent functor preserves a class of colimits if it sends every colimiting cocone in that class to a colimiting cocone.
